neighbours.label: 'to' / 'in' right after a travel or stay phrase, where a destination is expected (our trip| to Italy, two weeks| in Vienna, moved| to Australia)
fire: During our honeymoon we flew to Greece and stayed by the sea.
Next spring my parents are moving to Canada for good.
I spent a lovely week in Lisbon eating pastries.
Our school organized a field trip to Washington last year.
After retiring, she relocated to Spain with her husband.
We booked a cheap holiday in Morocco for October.
He took a weekend getaway to the mountains with friends.
The band went on a long tour in Europe last summer.
quiet: During our honeymoon we listened to music and stayed by the sea.
Next spring my parents are going to retire for good.
I spent a lovely week eating pastries and reading.
Our school organized a bake sale last year for charity.
After retiring, she talked to her husband about gardening.
We booked a cheap table for dinner on Friday.
He took a long nap with the dog on the sofa.
The band was interested in jazz from the start.

notes: Probe: 'a trip to' 0.67 whether or not a place follows; 'three weeks in' 0.42 even before 'bed'. So it is predictive: it fires on the preposition when travel sets up a destination. Output promotes place-name starts (Ban, Sant, Amsterdam).
